title: Fit all six nozzle bodies on a sprayer boom with the 02 size, by the ISO colour code
instruction: The job card calls for size 02 flat-fan nozzles. Make each of the six black nozzle bodies on the sprayer boom hold one 02 nozzle standing upright in it, telling the sizes apart by the ISO colour code. The 02s already fitted can stay. Put every nozzle of another size that you take off the boom into one of the two white parts trays, and fit 02s from the spares on the grey pads. Leave no nozzle anywhere else.
context: Crop sprayer operators (O*NET 37-3012 pesticide handlers, sprayers and applicators; 45-2091 agricultural equipment operators) check the boom's nozzles before every job. Spray nozzles are colour-coded by size (flow rate) under ISO 10625: 01 orange, 015 green, 02 yellow, 025 lilac, 03 blue, 04 red, 05 brown, 06 grey, 08 white. The job's application rate and forward speed fix one size, and every nozzle on the boom must be that size: a mixed boom sprays unevenly, over-dosing under the larger nozzles and leaving under-dosed stripes under the smaller ones. So the operator leaves the nozzles that are already the right size, takes the wrong ones off into a parts tray (apart from the new spares, so they are not refitted by mistake) and fits the right size from the spares. Here the scene never shows the code: the robot must know that 02 is yellow and tell it from its neighbours in the code, orange 01 among the spares and lilac 025 on the boom.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Everything is fixed except the thirteen nozzles. (1) Boom: a grey aluminium bar, 44 x 680 x 25 mm (680 mm along y), centred at x 32.0 cm, y 0, standing in for a bench section of a crop sprayer's boom. (2) Six nozzle bodies: black plastic square sockets fixed on the boom's top, each four walls 5 mm thick and 8 mm tall round a 32 x 32 mm opening (42 x 42 mm outside), centred on the boom's centre line at x 32.0 cm and y +31.25, +18.75, +6.25, -6.25, -18.75 and -31.25 cm, 125 mm apart (a real boom spaces them 500 mm). From the robot's left they are called L3, L2, L1, R1, R2 and R3. (3) Two parts trays: white open plastic boxes 100 x 100 mm and 25 mm tall outside, with a 5 mm floor and 5 mm walls (90 x 90 mm and 20 mm deep inside), centred at x 20.0 cm, y +11.0 and -11.0 cm. (4) Two spares pads: grey PVC plates 100 x 110 x 5 mm (100 mm along x), centred at x 17.75 cm, y +26.5 and -26.5 cm. (5) Nozzles: thirteen loose solid acetal (POM) cylinders 22 mm across and 32 mm tall, 17 g each, standing in for nozzle tips and coloured by ISO 10625 size: yellow, blue, lilac, red, green and orange. At the start all stand upright. In the bodies: L3 yellow, L2 blue, L1 empty, R1 lilac, R2 yellow, R3 blue, each centred in its body on the boom's top. On the pads, four spares each in two rows (x 15.0 and 20.5 cm) and two columns (y 23.5 and 29.5 cm either side of the midline), centres in cm: left pad: yellow at x 15.0, y 23.5; red at x 15.0, y 29.5; green at x 20.5, y 23.5; yellow at x 20.5, y 29.5; right pad: orange at x 15.0, y -23.5; yellow at x 15.0, y -29.5; yellow at x 20.5, y -23.5; red at x 20.5, y -29.5. So each pad holds exactly the two 02s its side of the boom needs. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Scored on the end state. A nozzle is 'in' a body, a tray or on a pad when its centre, seen from above, is over the body's 32 x 32 mm opening, the tray's 90 x 90 mm inside or the pad's 100 x 110 mm top, and its lowest point is less than 40 mm above the boom's top, the tray's floor or the pad's top (standing, lying, or resting on another nozzle there). Anywhere else (on the table or in the air, on the boom outside the body openings, or 40 mm or more above a body, tray or pad) it is 'loose'; with its centre below the table's top or beyond its edge it is 'off the table'. A nozzle is 'fitted' when it is in a body, stands upright (axis within 10 degrees of vertical, either end down) with its lowest point within 3 mm of the boom's top, and is still (its centre moved 2 mm or less, as a path, over the last 0.5 s). Only the nozzles' poses count, whether or not a gripper still holds one. Sizes by ISO 10625 colour: 01 orange, 015 green, 02 yellow, 025 lilac, 03 blue, 04 red; the job needs 02. Score 0 if any nozzle is off the table, if any body holds two or more nozzles, or if L3 or R2 (the two that start with an 02) does not hold a fitted 02 at the end. Otherwise 0.25 for each of L2, L1, R1 and R3 that holds one nozzle, a fitted 02; the total is at most 0.5 while any body holds a nozzle of another size (fitted or not: the boom is still mixed), and at most 0.75 while any nozzle is loose or a blue or lilac nozzle (the sizes that come off the boom; no spare is blue or lilac) is on a spares pad. Spares may stay on their pads or go into either tray, and removed nozzles into either tray, standing or lying. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 and 1.0 (for example: the start 0; only L1 filled 0.25; L2 and L1 done with R1's lilac and R3's blue still in place 0.5; three bodies done and R1 emptied but not refilled 0.75; every body done but a removed nozzle left on the table 0.75; an orange fitted in R1 for an 02, everything else right, 0.5; everything right 1.0). Only the end state counts: an 02 taken out of L3 and put back, or replaced by another 02, scores the same as one left alone. The trial ends early once 1.0 has held for 2.5 s; otherwise it is scored as it stands at the run limit. In a real trial, a top photo shows each nozzle's colour and where it stands, and a square held against a nozzle shows its tilt.
fidelity: A bench mock-up of a boom section: open square sockets on the bar's top, 125 mm apart (a sprayer's bodies hang under the boom, 500 mm apart), and plain colour-coded acetal cylinders, larger than real tips (about 15 mm across), standing loose in them with no thread, bayonet cap, seal or strainer, so 'fitted' means upright on the boom's top inside a socket. No liquid is used; spray, flow and wear are not simulated. Rigid bodies, default friction.
reset_notes: Stand the nozzles back upright, centred: in the bodies L3 yellow, L2 blue, R1 lilac, R2 yellow, R3 blue, L1 empty; on the left pad yellow (x 15.0, y 23.5 cm), red (15.0, 29.5), green (20.5, 23.5), yellow (20.5, 29.5); on the right pad orange (15.0, -23.5), yellow (15.0, -29.5), yellow (20.5, -23.5), red (20.5, -29.5). Empty both trays. Nothing is consumed; the boom, bodies, trays and pads are fixed.
